claims.text: St James's Palace is the most senior royal palace in London and officially remains the principal seat of the British monarch.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace was built in the 1530s by order of King Henry VIII on the former site of an isolated leper hospital dedicated to Saint James the Less.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Its distinctive architecture is primarily Tudor in style and was constructed mainly using traditional red brick.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the Tudor and Stuart eras, it was surrounded by a deer park and often served as a quiet hunting lodge and retreat from the formal court.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace took on primary administrative functions for the monarchy only after the main Palace of Whitehall tragically burned down.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1809, a devastating fire destroyed significant parts of the building, including the monarch's private apartments which were never replaced.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The building eventually began losing its status as the monarch's primary residence, a move that was formalized in 1837 by Queen Victoria in favor of Buckingham Palace.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Because it is still the official court, all foreign ambassadors and high commissioners to the United Kingdom are officially accredited to the Court of St James's.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The palace remains an active working residence today, housing the London apartments of several members of the royal family, including Princess Anne.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The nearby Queen's Chapel, designed by the famous architect Inigo Jones in the 1620s, is still considered to be an integral part of the palace complex.
claims.subject: self
